items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. So like I feel very privileged to have lived during this particular era. Because a lot of the young musicians, they do no, well not all of them, but a lot of them don’t do any research. Now I’ll tell you, I had a chance to meet John Coltrane when he was with Dizzy. And I had met him before that, in fact I met him with Eddie “Cleanhead” Vinson. But he of course, he wasn’t playing the way he was when he [inaudible]. But he could play the blues. I’m talking about play some real blues. And on one of his…

No, no, no, the one that they both worked with Cannonball, oh that was it, Cannonball. Now they played a blues, and let me tell you, they were playing the real funk, stunk down, knock me down blues, you know. And that’s what you don’t hear too much. See so although they did play other things, they were able to play that because of the fact that they had this blues background. And that’s what’s very important. And when you don’t get a chance to experience playing the blues, you really just, you really don’t have…
